admission.justification: Three owners build, join and publish one queue, and the class and subject fields are what make a row actionable rather than merely visible. A dropped kind or a row without its subject is silent in the data and visible only to the developer who needed it, which the mixed-queue and navigation cases pin.

applicability: The single server-built attention queue, its served row contract and the Operations bell that renders it.
conditions: Each native kind has one builder beside the surviving operational builders, and one total sort ranks them all.
A live cause is a warning that clears only when its native cause ends and cannot be acknowledged; a terminal notice is an information row acknowledged once per occurrence.

A row carries the canonical task key and reference where one resolves and the actual agent where the row concerns an agent; a taskless agent's row carries no task, and an operational row located by provider, repository or enclosure alone carries no task or agent control at all.
exclusions: Restoring a provider input or kind that MIK-R199 removes.
Client-side ordering, grouping or a second interpretation of attention facts.
Inventing a task for a taskless seat.

origin.handoffEntry: curator:MIK-R200@v1 rules 1, 7 and 8 — one queue, five native kinds, an actionable row

statement: The Operations attention queue publishes the five native kinds beside the operational kinds that survive provider removal, through one server-built interpretation that keeps its severity ordering and stable tie-break. Every row says whether it is an action or a notice and whether it can be acknowledged, and a row that carries a task or an agent opens that exact subject.
